locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: Substrate is the N-ethylcyclopentylamine molecular ion (the page draws C2H5NH- on a five-membered ring with '+.' printed on the nitrogen), so the precursor mapped_smiles localizes charge and odd electron on N(1). Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the odd electron on N(1) into the N(1)-C(2) bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the ring C(2)-C(6) sigma bond into that same N(1)-C(2) bond, which rises to the immonium double bond. The undrawn move 3 carries the second electron of the cleaved ring bond onto C(6); the book simply prints the radical dot on that carbon in the next structure. Because the cleaved bond is IN the ring, this alpha step only OPENS the ring - no mass is lost yet - giving the distonic ion C2H5-N+H=CH-CH2CH2CH2-CH2. (the text calls this 'radical-site-initiated ring-opening [that] separates the radical and charge sites'). Map numbers: 1 = N, 2 = ring carbon bonded to N, 3 = its retained ring neighbour (the later H donor), 4 and 5 = the two intervening CH2 groups, 6 = the ring carbon cleaved off C(2), 7/8 = the N-ethyl CH2/CH3, 9 = the migrating hydrogen (written as the isotope-tagged explicit atom [1H:9] so that the H can carry an atom map at all - RDKit folds an untagged mapped H into implicit valence).

locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: The arrow is labelled 'rH' on the page. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the radical dot on the terminal carbon C(6) reaching down-left to the hydrogen, which the book writes out explicitly as 'H' on C(3); drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from that C(3)-H bond back up to C(6), i.e. into the C(6)-H bond being formed. The undrawn move 3 leaves the second electron of the old C(3)-H bond on C(3), which is why the next structure simply carries the dot there. Net: a 1,4-hydrogen shift (five-membered transition state counting C6-C5-C4-C3 plus the H) that relocates the radical site next to the immonium carbon while the terminal CH2. becomes CH3. Both C-H bonds are visible to the arrow bookkeeping here because the migrating hydrogen is mapped as [1H:9].

locator.section: 8.9 Decompositions of cyclic structures ("Three bonds cleaved")

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the radical on C(3) into the forming C(3)=C(4) pi bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the C(4)-C(5) sigma bond into that same pi bond. The undrawn move 3 puts the second electron of the cleaved C(4)-C(5) bond on C(5) - the book prints the expelled fragment as 'CH3 / .CH2', i.e. the ethyl radical, without drawing that hook. Products: the conjugated immonium ion C2H5-N+H=CH-CH=CH2 at m/z 84 (100%, the ion labelled on the page) plus C2H5.. Three bonds have now been cleaved in total (the ring C-C, the C-H, and this C-C), which is exactly the 'Three bonds cleaved' heading under which the page places this equation. The migrating hydrogen [1H:9] leaves with the ethyl radical, so relative to a hypothetical H-free two-bond ring cleavage the ion is one hydrogen lighter; that is recorded as hydrogen_shift = -1 on the peak.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for equation 8.63 (chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14); no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. The natural candidate for the first step, IMS_4_43_ (DFS '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[N+.]8([H]9)[C]10([H]11)([H]12)[C]13([H]14)([H]15)[H]16>>[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[N+]8([H]9){=}[C]10([H]11)([H]12).[C.]13([H]14)([H]15)[H]16'), was CHECKED: its geometry is right (the cleaved C(10)-C(13) bond is incident to the pi-forming carbon C(10)) but it does NOT match this substrate. It demands a CH2-CH3 arm on BOTH sides of the nitrogen; N-ethylcyclopentylamine offers one such arm (RDKit: SMARTS [N+][CH2][CH3] -> 1 match, the N-ethyl group) but the ring alpha carbon carries only a single hydrogen, so the full pattern fails (SMARTS [CH3][C;H2,H3][N+]([C;H2,H3][CH3]) -> 0 matches). Had it matched, it would in any case have cleaved the ethyl C-C to give (M-CH3)+, not the drawn ring-opening. No indexed rule performs the subsequent 1,4-rH on a distonic amine ion either (IMS_4_37_rH / IMS_4_38_rH move an H to a hydroxyl OXYGEN of an even- or odd-electron oxonium, not between two carbons). The page prints '100%' beside m/z 84 as a bare percentage without naming the experiment; it is the book's standard 70 eV EI value (running head '8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation') and ms_context is set accordingly.
